monthly_review.summary: This month shows a clear shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR and pace intensity — though total volume and session count are meaningfully lower than last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 now accounts for 82% of this month’s training vs only 55% last month, while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 2% — indicating a deliberate, underpinned aerobic base-building phase.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.3 more km across 3 additional sessions in the remaining 15 days to match last month’s volume — averaging 3.1 km per session. Prioritize consistency over intensity: even 3x 3–4 km Zone 2 runs will close the gap.

insights.title: Efficiency dip despite cadence gain
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.43 m/sec per bpm this month, even as cadence rose from 142 to 144 spm — suggesting recent faster efforts (e.g., 2026-05-16 at 447 sec/km pace) may be taxing efficiency without sufficient recovery or pacing discipline.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold & VO2 work
insights.body: Z4 and Z5 combined represent just 2% of this month’s training (vs 19% last month), with zero Z5 effort recorded — a meaningful reduction in high-end stimulus that may limit future pace resilience if sustained beyond 4–6 weeks.

insights.title: Stride length surged during high-HR effort
insights.body: On 2026-05-16 (HR 148 bpm, pace 447 sec/km), stride length jumped to 94.35 m — +27% above your May average (74.2 m) — likely reflecting form breakdown or overstriding under fatigue, supported by lowest ground contact time (286 ms) and highest vertical oscillation (8.1 cm) of recent runs.

insights.title: Back-to-back moderate-effort days show adaptive response
insights.body: The 2026-05-12 (HR 138) → 2026-05-13 (HR 135) pair shows stable HR and rising cadence (149→150 spm) despite similar pace (~9:30/km), suggesting improved neuromuscular efficiency and recovery capacity within 24h — a positive sign of aerobic maturation.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm) at consistent 9:30–10:00/km pace, focusing on cadence ≥146 spm and minimizing vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm).
recommendations.reason: Your May avg HR is 135 bpm and Zone 2 dominance is intentional — this reinforces aerobic discipline while anchoring form metrics observed in your most efficient recent runs (e.g., 2026-05-13: 150 spm, 7.7 cm VO).

recommendations.action: Insert one 20-min progressive run in your next week: start at Z2 (HR 125–135), build to upper Z3 (HR 145–149) for final 6 min, monitoring ground contact time — aim to hold ≤320 ms throughout.
recommendations.reason: Your longest run was 9.5 km at HR 131 (Z2), and your best pace (428 sec/km) came last month — reintroducing controlled Z3 bridges aerobic base to pace readiness without triggering form breakdown like on 2026-05-16.

recommendations.action: After any run with HR ≥145 bpm, perform 5 min of post-run walk + 3x 30-sec single-leg balance holds (eyes open) per leg to reinforce neuromuscular control after fatigue.
recommendations.reason: The 2026-05-16 run showed elevated vertical oscillation (8.1 cm) and low ground contact (286 ms), signaling compromised stability — targeted balance work counters this specific fatigue signature.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthen the connection between heart rate discipline, cadence consistency, and running economy — using Zone 2 as the foundation while carefully reintroducing short, controlled Z3 stimuli to maintain neuromuscular engagement.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 tempo (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥146 spm)
20-min progressive run (Z2 → upper Z3, GC time ≤320 ms)
3 km easy + 4x 1-min Z1 strides with focus on silent footstrike and 7.2 cm vertical oscillation target
